newsitem.title: FRANCE: IMF CHIEF CAUTIONS ON YEN FALL -LE MONDE INTERVIEW.
newsitem.headline: IMF CHIEF CAUTIONS ON YEN FALL -LE MONDE INTERVIEW.

text.p: International Monetary Fund chief Michel Camdessus said in an interview in the French daily Le Monde on Friday that he believed world currency levels were normalising and could last.
"It is not surprising that the dollar is so robust at the time when the American economy itself is strong," he said.

"This leads me to believe that there is a normalisation of the international monetary constellation which has a chance of lasting because it is based on fundamental elements," Le Monde quoted Camdessus as telling its Washington correspondent in an interview.
Camdessus also said that the Japanese yen should not fall on a scale which would require the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates.
"The yen should not continue to fall to an extent that would lead the central bank to raise interest rates because that would have the effect of putting the brakes on growth," he said.
Japan had been especially shaken by the crisis in its financial sector, suggesting it would have to consolidate it during several years.
To stave off recession in the past five years, Japan has had to make a major effort to provide fiscal stimulus to growth, he said.
